conventions.scope: Shared types for Ares behavior parameters. JSON representations are serialization conventions; Python objects require runtime resolution.
conventions.union: A | B accepts either type. Optional[T] means T | null; nullability does not make a parameter optional. Only a constructor default makes it optional.
conventions.containers: list[T], set[T], tuple[T1, T2] and dict[K, V] preserve element types. Units is distinct from list[Unit]. Empty collections are allowed unless a parameter requires otherwise.
conventions.aliases: UnitID = UnitTypeId; np.ndarray = Grid; None = null; typing.List/Set/Tuple/Dict normalize to list/set/tuple/dict; Union[A, B] normalizes to A | B.
conventions.enums: Serialize enum member names, not display names. Valid members come from the installed enum; action-specific allowed values are a separate constraint.
conventions.references: Unit references identify current game entities. Availability, ownership, map bounds and ability compatibility are checked against the current game state.

tuple[T1, T2].meaning: Exactly two values, typed in order.

dict[K, V].meaning: Typed key-value mapping; JSON keys are strings.

Unit.meaning: Observation ID of a live unit (not a type or count).

Point2.meaning: Map coordinates or an available landmark name.

Grid.meaning: Runtime pathing/influence grid; never a model-made matrix.

UnitTypeId.meaning: Unit/structure type enum (not a live unit).

AbilityId.meaning: Ability enum; actor must have it ready.

Behavior.meaning: Nested child behavior (runtime-compiled, not a model expression).

ArmyComposition.meaning: Unit type -> {proportion, priority}; proportions sum to 1.

ResourcePair.meaning: Two thresholds in order: minerals, vespene.

ActionTimes.meaning: Worker tag -> last action time (game seconds); runtime bookkeeping.
